Figure 2. Hydrolysis reaction energy of sulfides, including 46 binary MS (grey circles), 52 ternary LiMS (green triangles) and 65 NaMS (orange triangles), as a function of cation M. More-negative reaction energy indicates worse moisture stability (moisture sensitive), whereas more-positive reaction energy indicates better moisture stability (moisture stable). The horizontal dashed lines correspond to the hydrolysis reaction energy of Li2S (green) and Na2S (orange), respectively. 17473 Angew. Chem. Int. figures.label: S1
figures.caption: Figure S1. Hydrolysis reactions for binary chlorides M-Cl, ternary lithium chlorides Li-M-Cl, and ternary sodium chlorides Na-M-Cl. The hydrolysis reactions are calculated using the same scheme as in Figure 2. Reaction energy is normalized to per H2O. The investigated compounds include M-Cl (grey circles), lithium ternary compounds Li-M-Cl (green triangles) and sodium ternary compounds Na-M-Cl (orange triangles). Compounds with more negative hydrolysis reaction energy are less stable against moisture, while compounds with more positive hydrolysis reaction energy are more stable against moisture. The horizontal dashed lines correspond to the hydrolysis reaction energy of LiCl (green) and NaCl (orange), respectively.
